tagline.text: Sorsogon's month-long October celebration of its founding as a province

location.label: Location
location.text: Rompeolas Baywalk and Kasanggayahan Amphitheater area, Sorsogon City, Bicol

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: October (especially around the mid-month founding anniversary and the end of the month)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1–2 days (during the month, pick the days you want)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,100–1,800 (based on a one-way bus fare from Manila; lodging and meals extra)

children.text: The Kasanggayahan Festival is Sorsogon's biggest annual event, held every October to mark the day on October 17, 1894 when Sorsogon split from Albay and became its own province. Parades, a national festival competition, concerts and an agro-industrial fair fill the city center.

The Kasanggayahan Festival is the signature festival that Sorsogon Province in the Bicol region holds every October. Sorsogon became a separate province from Albay on October 17, 1894, and the festival commemorates that founding. The first festival was held in 1974 under Governor Juan Frivaldo, and it is said to be organized by the provincial government together with the Kasanggayahan Foundation. According to the provincial government, October 17 is a special holiday across the province under a 1993 law.

The name is said to come from an old Bicol word meaning prosperity, abundance and a contented life. Some explanations describe it as a time when the fields are green, the rivers and sea are full of fish and homes are at peace. For that reason the festival is less a religious event than a thanksgiving celebration of the year's harvest and the region's growth. The Philippine Tourism Promotions Board (TPB) calendar lists it as October 1–31, which shows it is not a single-day event but a festival in which many events run through the whole month.

The main stage is Sorsogon City. Places often mentioned are the Rompeolas Baywalk along the bay, Magsaysay Street and Rizal Street, and the Kasanggayahan Amphitheater beside the playground shared by Sorsogon National High School and Sorsogon State University. The amphitheater is said to have been built in 1974, the year of the first festival. The program and timing change from year to year, so the most accurate approach is to check the provincial government's official announcements before you visit.

The events fall into roughly three groups. The first is the Festival of Festivals competition and parades, where Bicol regional and national festivals compete. The second is the nightly concerts, comedy shows and beauty pageant. The third is the agro-industrial fair and the Kasanggayahan Tiangge, a food and goods market. It is far from Manila and not many foreign tourists come, but the big advantage is that you can watch Filipinos enjoy a local festival up close.
Pantomina sa Tinampo, a Bicolano courtship dance sometimes called the dance of the doves, is the symbol of this festival. Wikipedia reports that on October 31, 2019, 7,127 people danced it over about
30 minutes
along a roughly
5 km
route in Sorsogon City, setting a Guinness World Record. The stage was reportedly the Rompeolas Baywalk, Magsaysay Street and Rizal Street.

A regional competition among festival groups from across Bicol and a national competition among groups from around the country are held. In 2024 the regional competition was announced for October 15 and the national competition for October 16. At the national competition, traditional dance groups perform at the Sorsogon Sports Complex, and the 2025 top prize was reported as ₱5 million.

This is the day Sorsogon became a province in its own right, and it is a special holiday across the province. Ceremonies and parades are reported to be held around this day, so it can be considered the heart of the festival. Because government offices and schools are closed, check local transport and business hours for that day.

In 2024, concerts and comedy shows featuring TJ Monterde, KZ Tandingan, Parokya ni Edgar and others were announced. Performers and dates change every year. Many shows take place near the amphitheater, so the city center is busiest in the evening.

This pageant is for women who promote the values of the provincial government's program areas (health, education, livelihood, infrastructure, tourism, environment, and peace and order). In 2024, 53 official candidates were chosen from 236 applicants. The glamorous costumes and stage design are the attractions.

The tiangge is an open-air market that sells local specialties, farm produce and food, and a trade fair is held as well. Sorsogon is known for pili nut products and Bicol cuisine, which makes it a good place to sample and shop. Prices vary by seller, so check on the spot.

blocks.title: Nearby local festivals and sports events

children.text: Reports say that during the month other events take place alongside it, such as the Paraw Festival Parade of Lights in Pilar, the Ginuman Festival in Sorsogon City, sports events such as biking and boat racing, and art events. Not every event is held every year, so it is safest to confirm with this year's published calendar.

items.title: Two-day, one-night plan
items.subtitle: City events by day, concerts at night

children.text: Arrive in Sorsogon City, drop off your bags at your lodging and walk along the Rompeolas Baywalk. Enjoy the coastline and bay views and have a light breakfast.

Check the city hall or provincial government Facebook page for any parade or competition announced that day, then head to the venue. Parades follow the roads, so you will get better photos from a stretch with fewer people.
Have lunch at the tiangge or a restaurant in town and try Bicol dishes. Buying specialties such as pili nut sweets now means carrying less later.
Escape the heat by visiting historic sights in town, such as the Sorsogon museum. These are covered in more detail in the Sorsogon City entry.
Watch a concert or comedy show near the amphitheater. Entry arrangements and fees differ by show, so check announcements in advance.
When the events end, return to your lodging on foot or by tricycle. It is safer to travel with companions late at night.
The event schedule changes each year, so the times above are an imaginary sample itinerary. Check the latest announcements from the provincial government and city hall before you visit.
Check that day's event calendar near Sorsogon City Hall.
If there is a parade or competition that day, go to that stretch and watch it; if not, walk the city's waterfront promenade.
For lunch, try a Bicol-style coconut milk dish at a restaurant near the market. Tell them how spicy you want it when you order.
Before sunset, enjoy the bay views near Rompeolas, then catch an evening event or head back to your lodging.

One festival guide suggests flying into the airport near Legazpi in Albay and taking a bus to Sorsogon. That means flying from Manila to Bicol International Airport (DRP, near Legazpi) and continuing overland.
We could not find bus or van fares and travel times from Legazpi to Sorsogon City in the sources we checked. Confirm them directly at the local terminal.
October is a rainy period, so flights can be delayed. It is best to allow some slack in your schedule.
Direct buses run from Manila to Sorsogon City. DLTB is listed at about

Travel time is listed at about
11–14 hours
depending on the operator and traffic, and there are reports of a trip taking 17 hours. Most people take an overnight bus.
Seats can fill up quickly during the festival, so booking ahead is a good idea.
Fares are the figures posted on booking sites and may have gone up recently.
Tricycles and jeepneys are the basic way to get around Sorsogon City. Fares depend on distance and haggling, so agree on the price before you board.
The venues are within walking distance of one another, but roads can be closed on parade days.

The festival is held in October, so the time to visit is effectively October. Within that month, the most popular periods are mid-month, when the regional and national competitions take place, the days around the October 17 founding anniversary, and the end of the month. The 2019 Guinness record event was also held on October 31.

October is near the end of the Philippine rainy season, but Bicol lies in the path of typhoons and rainy days are common. Bring an umbrella or a light rain jacket, and keep in mind that outdoor events can be canceled or postponed. Regional travel guides likewise agree that October is rainy.

Sorsogon City has hotels and guesthouses in town and lodging near the bay. During the festival, rooms fill up quickly, especially around the competitions and the founding anniversary. We could not confirm any long-established lodging names in this research, so check recent reviews and locations on booking sites and choose a place within walking distance of the venues.

As is typical of Bicol, the food centers on spicy dishes made with coconut milk and chili. Sorsogon is also known for pili nut products, which are worth sampling at the tiangge. If you are worried about hygiene, choose freshly cooked food from busy stalls.
Before you go, check the latest event calendar from the Sorsogon provincial government and city hall (official website and Facebook). The calendar is sometimes posted only as an image.
If you want to see the competitions or parades, aim for the days around mid-month (October 15–17) and book your lodging and bus in advance.
The venues are crowded. Carry cash in small amounts split across pockets.
Prepare for October rain with an umbrella, a waterproof bag and a change of clothes.
When photographing parades, follow the guidance of those around you on photographing performers.
Overnight buses from Manila are heavily air-conditioned, so long sleeves are handy.
City sights such as the Sorsogon museum and churches are best visited at times when no event is on.
Schedules and prices can change, so check the latest announcements.

October is typhoon and heavy rain season in Bicol. If a weather warning is issued, outdoor events may be canceled or postponed, so check the forecast and local government announcements before and during your trip.
Event dates, venues and performers change every year. The examples in this article are based on 2024 announcements.
On event days roads are closed and traffic is heavy, and you should watch out for pickpockets.
Do not travel alone on isolated roads at night.
Bicol is volcano (Mayon, Bulusan and others) and typhoon country, so check government disaster information when traveling outside the city.
Bus fares and travel times can vary widely depending on the operator.
The provincial capital and the stage for the festival. You can explore the city's museum, churches and the Rompeolas Baywalk on foot.
